adjudicator: Claude Code — JUDGEMENT, not a scorer output
method: Each of the 19 differing replies read against the ground_truth carried on its row (expected_sw for the diverted set, expected_behavior for the natural 48, correct_answer_sw for the prior-decision rows) and against CLAUDE.md section 11 / scripts/locked_facts.json where the corpus carries none. 'The answer changed' is not 'the answer improved'. Severity is recorded separately from direction, because a weak preference and a wrong-answer flip must not cancel in a tally.
headline: NEITHER ARM WINS. 4 decisive rows to two-arm, 3 decisive rows to single-arm, and the three single-arm wins only became visible because this measurement included the rows the prior decision rests on. Yesterday's 4/2/7 was itself population-limited — R22 applied to my own measurement one day later.

the_correction_that_matters_most.what: The 2026-08-24 measurement (eval/results/two_arm_effect.json) drew its population from the veto-diverted rows and the natural 48 ONLY. It reported 4 two-arm better / 2 single-arm better / 7 equivalent, with BOTH decisive wins going to two-arm and BOTH single-arm wins being wrong->wrong.
the_correction_that_matters_most.why_that_was_incomplete: The rows on which the two-arm retriever is KNOWN to harm were not in that population. They live in the 400-question gate corpus, which that measurement did not sample. Adding them moves the decisive count from 2:0 in two-arm's favour to 4:3 — roughly halving the case.
the_correction_that_matters_most.the_shape: This is R22 one level up, and it is the third instance in three days plus this fourth: a measurement drawn from where the mechanism looked good. It was caught only by deliberately re-running the prior decision's own cited rows, which is now R22's closing clause: a settled decision's age is not evidence, so re-run what it cites rather than re-reading its summary.

prior_cost.note: eval_208; eval_127 is the other and arrives via the diverted set

determinism_control.reading: 27 rows received byte-identical fact sets from both retrievers and returned byte-identical replies from both arms. The predecessor's stage-1 exclusion was therefore sound, and greedy decoding (do_sample: false, R14) is confirmed deterministic end-to-end over the live endpoint rather than assumed. A FAILED control would have been a non-empty list here, and would have invalidated every paired A/B in this repo.

r24_baselines.reading: 62 of 65 rows carrying a recorded live reply reproduced it BYTE-IDENTICALLY through the single-arm arm. That is the proof this harness is production and not a reconstruction of it — the failure mode R24 exists for. The 8 NO_BASELINE rows are the prior-decision rows, which have no recorded reply on the current pipeline at all; they are unverified rather than verified, and that is stated rather than glossed.

the_three_failures_and_an_earlier_claim_.the_correction: On 2026-08-24 I attributed these three to ROUTING-GAP-A/B having moved them to the compute path after their replies were recorded. THAT IS WRONG ON THE FACTS. All three were ALREADY labelled 'compute' in the 2026-08-17 adjudication and all three are on the compute path today, which is why the mechanical staleness rule does not excuse any of them.
the_three_failures_and_an_earlier_claim_.what_actually_happened: The compute path itself changed in the seven days since, and the CONTENT of each change says so: nat_23 now answers BOTH unlabelled levies (SDL 192,500 AND NSSF 1,100,000) where the recorded reply answered only NSSF — the D-DECOMP-1 fan-out; nat_05 now correctly names payroll as the SDL base where the recorded reply returned a BRELA registration fee; nat_24 no longer mis-attributes 10% to WCF, the exact defect D-FIDELITY-6 was built for. All three recorded verdicts were WRONG; two now look correct.
the_three_failures_and_an_earlier_claim_.what_that_says_about_the_rule: The path-comparison staleness rule is a LOWER BOUND. It detects only staleness that surfaces as a path change, and none of these did. It is kept because it is mechanical and cannot be argued with, not because it is complete — and its incompleteness is why every failure is listed individually with its content evidence instead of being swept into a count.
the_three_failures_and_an_earlier_claim_.does_it_affect_the_A_B: No. Both arms ran today against the same deployment, so the contrast is unaffected. Only the seven-day-old reference is stale.

r24_baselines.an_instrument_bug_found_mid_run: baseline_verdict originally tested the staleness rule BEFORE byte-identity, so seven rows (nat_10/15/20/25/26/36/38) whose replies reproduced EXACTLY were thrown out because two path labels disagreed. An exclusion rule may only ever excuse a mismatch, never discard a match. Fixed in bb373ac and re-derived offline via --rescore, which was possible only because the harness persists the evidence rather than the conclusion.

direction_tally.note: 19 differing rows of 73. The decisive counts are the ones that carry weight; the weak rows are preferences between two imperfect answers and are reported for completeness, not to pad a side.

the_guard_row.purpose: the rank-3 EFD fact the rejected INTERLEAVE merge evicted; the standing check that the shipped append-only merge cannot drop a baseline fact
the_guard_row.merge_verdict: APPEND-ONLY HOLDS. Both arms retrieve the same first three facts; two-arm appends a fourth. Nothing was dropped, which is what this row exists to check.
the_guard_row.but: ⚠️ BOTH ARMS ANSWER THE ROW WRONG. Sales of TZS 10,999,000 against an TZS 11,000,000 EFD threshold: single-arm says 'Ndiyo, kwa kuwa umefikia kizingiti cha mauzo cha milioni 11', two-arm says 'Ndiyo, kwa mauzo hayo unatakiwa kutumia EFD'. The corpus expectation is the opposite — 10,999,000 is BELOW the threshold and EFD is not yet mandatory. Earlier entries record this row as resolved (2026-08-11).
the_guard_row.why_it_is_a_separate_finding: It is not a retrieval failure. The correct threshold IS retrieved and single-arm even states it correctly — it then compares the user's figure against it wrongly. D-FIDELITY-7 checks whether a STATED threshold matches the statute and would pass this body, because the stated threshold is right. The defect is the COMPARISON.
the_guard_row.and_it_is_buildable: Under R19 this is a CONSTANT comparison, not a derived quantity: 10,999,000 < 11,000,000 is decidable from the user's own stated figure and a fixed statutory number, and no lawful transformation makes 'you have reached it' true. So a guard of the form 'if the body asserts the user has crossed a threshold, compare their stated figure against the statutory one' is buildable, works on the fact path, and needs no ComputationResult.

recommendation.verdict: KEEP SINGLE-ARM. Do not switch production.
recommendation.and_close_the_question: The 2026-08-17 decision is now settled ON EVIDENCE rather than by its own age, which is what it lacked. It should not be re-opened again without a new mechanism — not merely a new population.
the_grounds: 4 decisive rows to two-arm, 3 decisive rows to single-arm. That is not a mandate, and it is nowhere near enough to justify an R16 cycle on the retrieval path.

BOTH ARMS FABRICATE, on different rows and in different ways. Two-arm invents regulatory content — a 90M VAT threshold that exists nowhere (eval_208), a withholding formula that exists nowhere (eval_034). Single-arm under-reports — the NSSF employer share as the total (eval_337), a deadline it holds but will not state (eval_343). Neither failure class is acceptable and switching trades one for the other.
The prior decision's cost evidence PARTLY HOLDS and the surviving half is the most severe row in the set. eval_208 reproduces verbatim seven days and an index regeneration later.

8 of the 19 differing rows are EQUIVALENT and several are equivalently WRONG — pic_04 (30% of turnover), eval_355 (EFD below threshold), eval_010 (an unstated crossing), eval_348 (a false premise endorsed). The retriever does not touch any of them.
recommendation.the_reframing_that_is_the_real_output: This measurement was scoped to answer 'which retriever?'. Its most useful finding is that THE RETRIEVER IS NOT THE LEVER. Across 73 rows the choice moves 19 replies and improves a net of one row on decisive readings, while the failures that remain — wrong bases, wrong comparisons, endorsed false premises, fabricated formulas — sit downstream of retrieval in both arms. Further effort on the retrieval slot is competing for the wrong defect.
recommendation.what_this_does_NOT_say: It does not say two-arm is worse. It does not say the eval_337 class is closed — that row is still wrong in production and still has its own board item. It says the evidence does not support paying for a switch, and that the question has now been asked properly enough to stop asking it.
follow_ons_this_measurement_surfaced: eval_355: both arms say EFD is mandatory at TZS 10,999,000. Earlier entries record this row as resolved. Needs its own check — is this a regression, or was the earlier resolution on a different path?

A threshold-COMPARISON guard is buildable under R19 (constant comparison, no ComputationResult needed) and would cover eval_355 and eval_010, which D-FIDELITY-7 cannot reach because the threshold they state is correct and the comparison is not.
